verdict.rationale: Trigger.dev ships an official MCP server, and its tools include getting task information and triggering task runs, so an external agent can invoke your workflows through it. However, it is framed as a developer-assistant server (search docs, deploy, monitor runs). It offers a generic trigger-task tool rather than publishing each workflow or connected-app action as its own named MCP tool. missing for 10: per-task MCP tool exposure with schemas, documented production/external-agent use (auth, scoping), independent or hands-on corroboration.
